$comment: Separation-of-duties (SoD) ruleset for Contoso Health (fictional). One rule = two sides; a person holding anything on side A AND anything on side B is in conflict.
PREVENTIVE: post-apply/Set-IncompatibleAccessPackages.ps1 turns the package/group parts into Entra incompatibleAccessPackages / incompatibleGroups links (blocks requests and new admin assignments).

DETECTIVE: 09-SoD-Report.ps1 evaluates EXISTING access (package assignments, group membership incl. transitive, directory roles incl. PIM-eligible) - incompatibility settings never remove access someone already holds (Microsoft Learn).
Every name must exist in access-catalog.json; 'planned' objects are reported as not evaluable, never as clean.

Regulatory drivers are what the control supports, not a claim that the regulation prescribes this exact pair. SOX applies only if Contoso's parent is publicly traded; otherwise SOX-style ICFR is adopted as the internal-control framework.

holdingSemantics.groups: direct or transitive member; for a PIM-for-Groups group also an ELIGIBLE member (they can activate)
holdingSemantics.directoryRoles: active (permanent or activated) or PIM-ELIGIBLE assignment, direct or through a role-assignable group
holdingSemantics.reviewerOfRecord: the manager of someone holding a tier-T2 (request-policy) package: ADR 0012 makes the requestor's manager the T2 reviewer. Detective only (09-SoD-Report.ps1); no Entra setting can prevent it

rules.name: Medication administration vs controlled-substance dispensing
rules.riskStatement: A person who administers medication and also dispenses controlled substances can divert doses and document the waste or override that hides it.
regulatoryDrivers: DEA 21 CFR 1301.71(a): effective controls and procedures to guard against theft and diversion of controlled substances
HIPAA 45 CFR 164.308(a)(4): information access management (access authorization)
rules.mitigatingControlIfException: Separate time-boxed override package (Microsoft's pattern for SoD exceptions) with 90-day expiry and monthly Pharmacy Director review; daily automated-dispensing-cabinet discrepancy report; every controlled-substance waste witnessed by a second licensed person.
rules.supersedes: The single nurse/pharmacy pair in modules/entitlement var.sod_incompatible_pairs (legacy post-apply/Set-AccessPackageSoD.ps1, now a shim for Set-IncompatibleAccessPackages.ps1).
rules.preventiveNote: Links sit only on the requestable packages: Pharmacy X {Nurse, ICU, ICU - Float Access, All-Nurses, All-ICU} and ICU - Float Access X {Pharmacy, App-Pharmacy-Dispensing-Users}. Nurse and ICU are birthright and never gated; a pharmacist whose HR record moves to Nursing or ICU is caught by 09-SoD-Report.ps1.

rules.name: Prescribe vs dispense
rules.riskStatement: A prescriber who can also dispense can issue and fill the same controlled-substance order with no independent check.
regulatoryDrivers: DEA 21 CFR 1306.04(a): a corresponding responsibility for proper prescribing rests with the pharmacist who fills the prescription
rules.mitigatingControlIfException: Any order written by the dispensing person needs verification by a second pharmacist before release; monthly prescriber-equals-dispenser report to the Pharmacy & Therapeutics committee.

rules.name: Order vs approve (pharmacist verification) of medication orders
rules.riskStatement: The person who enters a medication order must not be the pharmacist who verifies it, or the independent appropriateness review does not happen.
regulatoryDrivers: CMS Conditions of Participation 42 CFR 482.25: pharmaceutical services (drugs controlled and distributed under pharmacy supervision)
verify: The Joint Commission MM.05.01.01 (pharmacist review of medication orders) - standard text is licensed, not checked here
rules.mitigatingControlIfException: EHR configured to block self-verification of one's own orders; weekly report of orders verified by their author reviewed by the Director of Pharmacy.

rules.name: Pharmacy inventory and purchasing vs dispensing
rules.riskStatement: Whoever orders, receives and adjusts controlled-substance inventory can hide a shortage created when dispensing.
regulatoryDrivers: DEA 21 CFR Part 1305: orders for Schedule I and II substances (DEA Form 222 / CSOS)
rules.mitigatingControlIfException: Blind count of receipts by a second person; biennial inventory taken by someone without dispensing rights; monthly perpetual-inventory reconciliation signed by the Pharmacy Director.

rules.name: Accounts payable processing vs vendor master data
rules.riskStatement: A person who can create or change a vendor (incl. bank details) and also process invoices can pay a fictitious or redirected vendor.
regulatoryDrivers: SOX section 404 (15 U.S.C. 7262): internal control over financial reporting - if applicable, else adopted ICFR
rules.mitigatingControlIfException: Weekly vendor-master change report reviewed by the Controller; bank-detail changes confirmed by call-back to a number already on file; positive pay with the bank.

rules.name: Payroll entry vs payroll approval
rules.riskStatement: A person who can enter pay changes and approve the payroll run can create ghost employees or raise their own pay.
regulatoryDrivers: SOX section 404 (15 U.S.C. 7262): internal control over financial reporting - if applicable, else adopted ICFR
rules.mitigatingControlIfException: Payroll register variance review by Finance every cycle; payroll system configured to block approving a run that contains one's own changes.

rules.name: EHR break-the-glass vs EHR audit-log administration
rules.riskStatement: Someone who can open any patient record in an emergency and also administer the audit trail can read PHI and suppress the evidence.

sideA.label: Can invoke EHR break-the-glass (every clinical bundle)

sideB.label: Administers the EHR audit trail (PIM for Groups)

regulatoryDrivers: HIPAA 45 CFR 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D): information system activity review
rules.mitigatingControlIfException: EHR audit trail streamed to the immutable (WORM) evidence store the admin cannot change; Privacy Office reviews every break-the-glass event within 1 business day; audit-admin activation needs Privacy Officer approval.
rules.preventiveNote: Nurse and ICU are birthright (never gated) and side B is a PIM group, so entitlement management can block only one direction: a member of PIM-EHR-AuditLog-Admins cannot request Prescriber or ICU - Float Access. verify: whether incompatibleGroups counts PIM-ELIGIBLE (not activated) members. Everything else in this pair is detective (09-SoD-Report.ps1).

rules.name: Identity administration vs access certification
rules.riskStatement: Someone who can create accounts or change group membership and also certifies access can grant access and then approve it in review.

sideB.label: Certifies or governs access, incl. as the reviewer of record (manager) of a direct report holding T2 access (ADR 0012)

regulatoryDrivers: HIPAA 45 CFR 164.308(a)(4)(ii)(B)-(C): access authorization; access establishment and modification
SOX section 404 IT general controls: independent user-access review - if applicable
rules.mitigatingControlIfException: Reviewers never see their own access (ADR 0012); a second-level review by the access governance lead of every decision the person made on access they provisioned; quarterly privileged review (T1) covers their eligibility.

rules.name: Charge entry and coding vs payment posting and adjustments
rules.riskStatement: A person who enters charges and also posts payments or writes off balances can conceal lapping or inappropriate write-offs, and upcoding goes unchecked.
regulatoryDrivers: SOX section 404 (15 U.S.C. 7262): internal control over financial reporting - if applicable, else adopted ICFR
False Claims Act 31 U.S.C. 3729: exposure from unchecked coding
rules.mitigatingControlIfException: Adjustments above a threshold need Billing Manager approval in the billing system; monthly write-off report reviewed by Revenue Cycle leadership.

exceptionsSchema.$comment: An approved exception (standards/exception-process.md) suppresses the violation from the exit code while unexpired; it stays listed in the report as 'excepted'. Expired = violation again.

example.compensatingControls: as approved in the exception register
